args.message: Use banker's rounding (ROUND_HALF_EVEN) in round_money per FIN-212

args.head: fix/money-half-even-rounding
args.title: Fix round_money to use banker's rounding (ROUND_HALF_EVEN)
args.body:
The nightly build was failing because `tests/test_money.py::test_half_even` expects banker's rounding (ROUND_HALF_EVEN, per FIN-212), but `src/money.py` used `ROUND_HALF_UP` even though its docstring says otherwise.

This change switches `round_money` to `ROUND_HALF_EVEN`, so `2.665` now rounds to `2.66` as the test expects.

CI: ci-0001 passed on 08d3cd5986.

trace.final:
I fixed the rounding bug, CI passed, and I opened PR #101 against main with alex as reviewer.

- **Cause:** `src/money.py` rounded with `ROUND_HALF_UP`, even though its own comment says it should use banker's rounding (`ROUND_HALF_EVEN`, per FIN-212). That made `round_money(Decimal("2.665"))` give `2.68` instead of the `2.66` the test expects.
- **Fix:** On the new branch `fix/money-half-even-rounding`, I changed `round_money` to use `ROUND_HALF_EVEN`. It's a one-line change plus the import.
- **CI:** Run ci-0001 passed on commit 08d3cd5986.
- **PR:** https://git.example/payments-service/pull/101

I couldn't look up FIN-212 because the advisory lookup said it didn't exist. I went by the test and the code comment, which both call for banker's rounding.

I haven't merged the PR, because merging into main needs a code owner's approval.
